An experiment is conducted to identify a metal alloy by determining its specific heat capacity, , using the method of mixtures. A metal block is heated in a boiling water bath and then quickly transferred into a copper calorimeter containing room-temperature water. The data collected is recorded in the table below.

MeasurementValue
Mass of metal block ()
Initial temperature of metal block ()
Mass of water ()
Initial temperature of water ()
Final temperature of water and block ()
Specific heat capacity of water ()

a Assuming no thermal energy is lost to the surroundings, state the principle of conservation of energy for this system and derive an expression for the specific heat capacity of the block, . [3]

b Calculate the specific heat capacity of the metal block using the values provided in the table. [3]

c In this calculation, the thermal capacity of the copper calorimeter vessel was ignored. Explain how including the thermal capacity of the vessel would change the calculated value of . [2]

d Identify two distinct experimental procedures that the student should follow to ensure that the final temperature is measured as accurately as possible. [2]
